_note: PLAN.md 9. All numbers are STARTING VALUES to be tuned by playtest.
MVP is two buildings (PLAN.md 10): a Town Centre to train from and a House
to raise the pop cap. Barracks and the dragon nest are later phases.
Each building names THREE visuals, not one. A building is a foundation, a
completed structure, or rubble (SimBuilding.Phase), and 0 A.D. models those
as separate actors -- so they are separate atlases, shared by footprint size:
vis.foundation_8x8 will serve every 8x8 building added later. There is no
under-construction art; the foundation covers that phase too, and 5.2 shows
progress by clipping the completed sprite over it (ASSET_MISSING.md 1.2).
FOOTPRINTS COME FROM THE MEASURED ART, not from PLAN.md 9's sketch, which
wrote [4, 4] for the town centre before anything had been measured. Measured
via `isobake inspect`, halved to project metres, divided by the 2 m tile:
town centre   15.53 x 15.00 m  = 7.77 tiles  -> [8, 8]  SUPERSEDED, below
house         10.00 x 10.00 m  = 5.00 tiles  -> [4, 4]   (see below)
Scaling a mesh down to fit a chosen footprint is not the alternative -- it
would break the one-global-pixels_per_metre rule (PLAN.md 2.2) and leave a
villager taller than the doorway.
FOOTPRINT IS THE MAX ACROSS ALL FOUR AGE SKINS (PLAN.md 13.2 item 10).
A building re-skins in place as its owner advances an age, so its footprint
cannot change with the skin -- it must claim what its age-4 form needs from
the moment it is placed. 0 A.D.'s civs do NOT agree on obstruction size, so
measured from simulation/templates/structures/<civ>/ at 4 units per tile:
age1 brit   age2 gaul   age3 achae   age4 rome   max
So the town centre is [10, 10], not the [8, 8] the Athenian actor measured at
0.4: the Roman age-4 civic centre is 37x37 and the Achaemenid one 38.5 wide.
The max is taken PER AXIS because buildings do not rotate. Decided 2026-08-14
by the project owner: fix the number once now rather than break every placed
town centre the day age 4 lands.
visual_foundation still points at vis.foundation_8x8, which is now one tile
small on each side -- the same deliberate art/gameplay disagreement the house
makes below, in the opposite direction. vis.foundation_10x10 is queued in
ASSET_MISSING.md 1.2; pointing at it before it is baked would only make the
foundation render as the loud magenta placeholder, which is worse than a
foundation that reads slightly small.
The house is the one place art and gameplay deliberately DISAGREE: the mesh
is 5 tiles across but the footprint is [4, 4], matching the 4x4 foundation
0 A.D. pairs it with. So the roof overhangs its own tiles by half a tile a
side. That is the right trade -- a 5x5 house is oddly large next to an 8x8
town centre, odd-sized footprints centre badly on a grid, and overhanging
roofs are normal in isometric RTS art. Revisit if placement collisions ever
look wrong rather than merely generous.
THE FULL ROSTER, added once the age bakes landed. Age & Unit Planning.md
is authoritative for which 0 A.D. structure each of these is in each age;
visuals.json holds the age->atlas map and this file holds only the stable
id, so nothing here changes when a skin is re-pointed.
FOOTPRINTS ARE STILL THE MAX ACROSS AGE SKINS, PER AXIS -- the rule the
town centre already followed. Measured the same way: each age's source
template resolved through its parent chain to <Obstruction><Static>, in
0 A.D. units at 4 per tile, rounded UP, then maxed. Written out so the
number can be re-derived rather than trusted:

house             3x3      3x3      4x4      4x4      [4, 4]
lumber camp       2x2      3x4      4x5      4x5      [4, 5]
mining camp       3x5      3x5      4x4      4x4      [4, 5]
barracks          --       5x5      5x5      6x6      [6, 6]
market            --       7x6      8x8      8x7      [8, 8]
blacksmith        --       5x5      5x5      5x5      [5, 5]
stable            --       5x5      5x4      5x5      [5, 5]
archery range     --       7x6      6x5      7x6      [7, 6]
watch tower       --       3x2      3x2      2x2      [3, 2]

FOUNDATIONS AND RUBBLE ARE SHARED BY SIZE, and only nine foundation and
seven rubble sizes are baked, so several buildings point at the nearest one
rather than an exact match -- the same deliberate art/gameplay disagreement
the house already makes. The town centre keeps vis.foundation_8x8 against a
[10, 10] footprint (vis.foundation_10x10 is still queued in ASSET_MISSING
1.2); the archery range's [7, 6] takes the 7x7 pad; monastery, university
and market take 8x8. Pointing at an unbaked id would only render the loud
magenta placeholder, which is worse than a foundation that reads a little
off. The house's rubble moves from vis.rubble_3x3 to vis.rubble_4x4 here --
it was on the 3x3 only because 4x4 had not been baked at 0.4.
WALLS AND GATES, added 2026-08-21 with the wall system (PLAN.md 5.8). They
were absent because a wall is not an ordinary building -- it needs drag
placement, automatic short/medium/long segment choice, an orientation, and a
gate that opens -- and declaring them as ordinary buildings would have put
twelve fixed-orientation blocks in the build menu. All four of those exist now.
The note that used to sit here also claimed the pieces were 'declared in
visuals.json', and they were not: only the tower's rubble and foundation were.
See visuals.json's own `_note_walls`.
TWELVE DEFS, THREE MENU ENTRIES. Each tier is four defs -- short, medium, long,
gate -- and only ONE of the four is offered: the short segment carries
`wall_lengths` and is the WALL entry (the drag reads that list and lays down
whichever lengths fit). The other three are `buildable: false`, a flag meaning
'the system may place this, the menu may not offer it'. Without it the build
grid would list all twelve.
THE GATE CAME OFF THAT MENU ON 2026-08-22 and became an UPGRADE, which is a fix
and not a restriction. It was a menu entry placed by tapping, and the project
owner found the hole in a day of playing: 'how do I rotate a gate?' You could
not. A gate is [9, 2], `PlaceBuildingCommand` carries no facing and never
transposes a footprint, so every tap-placed gate lay east-west -- and a
NORTH-SOUTH WALL COULD NOT HAVE A GATE IN IT AT ALL.
So the long segment now carries `upgrades_to` and you convert one where it
stands. That does not answer the rotation question, it deletes it: the wall
already knows which axis it was dragged along and the gate inherits its origin,
footprint and facing. See `UpgradeBuildingCommand`. The target must declare the
SAME footprint -- validated, not trusted -- because the conversion keeps the
ground the building already holds, and that is also why only the LONG piece
carries the field: a 3x2 short segment has nowhere to put a 9x2 gate.
FOOTPRINTS, and this is the one pleasant surprise in the whole feature: every
civ 0 A.D. bakes a wall from agrees on the segment lengths. Measured the usual
way -- <Obstruction><Static> in 0 A.D. units at 4 per tile, rounded up, maxed
per axis across the tier's ages:
germ      brit      achae     rome      tiles
wall short      12x8      12x6      12x6      12x8      [3, 2]
wall medium     24x8      24x6      24x6      24x8      [6, 2]
wall long       36x8      36x6      36x6      36x8      [9, 2]
wall gate       37x6.5    36x7      36x6      36x6      [9, 2]  see below
So 3 / 6 / 9 tiles long and 2 deep, universally, and the tier is nothing but a
skin and a price. That is what makes one segmentation function correct for all
three tiers.
THE GATE IS FORCED TO A LONG SEGMENT'S [9, 2] even though the germ one measures
9.25 tiles wide. A gate has to be substitutable for a long segment or it cannot
sit in a wall run without leaving a gap -- 0 A.D. makes the gate an UPGRADE of a
long wall for exactly this reason. The cost is a half-tile of art overhang, the
same deliberate art/gameplay disagreement the house's roof already makes.
HP IS PER 3-TILE SEGMENT, so a long wall is worth exactly three short ones and
there is no cheapest-per-tile way to wall a town: wood 400, stone 600,
reinforced 900 for every 3 tiles. 0 A.D.'s own numbers (1000/2000/3000) are on a
different scale to ours -- our town centre is 2000 -- and a long wall tougher
than a town centre would be a wall nothing in the roster can break. Gates are
5/6 of the wall they replace: a door is the weak point, and it gives an attacker
something better to hit than 9 tiles of stone.
COSTS FOLLOW THE ROSTER'S MATERIAL, which is the whole difference between the
tiers: wood walls cost wood ('wall Lumber'), stone and reinforced cost stone.
Per 3 tiles: wood 12, stone 15, reinforced 25. Gates add wood for the doors.
`los: 3` on a segment is deliberately small. A wall you cannot see past is odd,
and a wall is also the cheapest possible tripwire -- but a 40-segment wall is 40
vision circles, and PLAN.md 14 already has a risk about vision being a tick cost
before it is a wire cost. Three tiles is 28 tiles a circle; a gate gets 5
because it is a gate you want to watch.
NO GARRISON. 0 A.D. walls hold turrets (its medium wall declares eight turret
points) and ours hold nobody -- garrison is 4.8 and unbuilt, and a wall is the
wrong place to introduce it.
THE WALL TOWER IS ALREADY HERE as `building.guard_tower`: the roster's
'Pers/wall_tower (Guard Tower)' and 'rome/wall_tower' are exactly what
vis.guard_tower is baked from. Nothing to add, and no wall-tower def -- 0 A.D.
auto-places towers at wall corners, which is a nicety that wants the wall system
settled first.
TRAINS IS THE BUILDING'S WHOLE LIST, NOT ITS LIST FOR ONE AGE. An archery
range trains archers from age 2 and crossbowmen from age 3, and that gate
belongs to the UNIT (units.json `age_required`), not to a per-age copy of
the building's roster -- otherwise every building would need four `trains`
lists and adding a unit would mean editing all four.
THERE IS NO `category` FIELD, AND THAT IS A DECISION. 19 buildings do not fit
the 4x3 detail grid, and an uncapped list would drop seven of them silently.
This file briefly carried a category to split the build menu in two; the
project owner chose PAGING instead (2026-08-16), so the grid pages with < and
> and every building stays in one list. That is the better answer here: a
split has to be maintained as a judgement per building and still caps out if
one side grows, where paging is arithmetic and holds for any roster size.
The ordering that replaces it is (age unlocked, then name), so the buildings
a player has had longest keep their position -- see SelectionActions.
THE FIELD, in full (project owner, 2026-08-17). It is the one building that is
also a resource node, and all four of its numbers are rules rather than stats:
blocks_movement false   the crop is NOT A WALL. It claims its 36 tiles so
nothing is built over them, and villagers walk on and across
it. Both of the reasons are really one: a 6x6 plot flush
against a 5x4 mill left no free tile to stand on to drop food
off, and no way onto the plot to spread the gatherers over it.
0 A.D.'s own fields are walked over too.
max_per_host_by_age [0, 2, 3, 4]   two plots to a mill at age 2, three at 3,
four at 4. The owner asked whether age 2 should really allow
all four; it should not -- four plots at the age-2 yield is
most of a town's food from one building the moment the age
lands. The roster's four is where a farm economy ENDS UP.
`max_per_host` stays as the flat fallback for anything that
declares no per-age list.
amount -1     it NEVER DEPLETES. This was 300 and the field was removed when
harvested out; the owner reversed that -- the balancing lever
is the yield, and a plot that had to be rebuilt every few
minutes made a mill's four fields into upkeep, not an economy.
-1 is BuildingDef.INFINITE_CROP; the finite path still works
and is still tested, for whatever wants it next.
slots 5       five villagers to a plot, and four plots to a mill
(max_per_host), so one mill absorbs twenty farmers at most.
age_required 2  there are no fields in age 1 at all.
yield_per_age  food per 100 ticks PER VILLAGER, by age: 0, 25, 28, 32.
BALANCED AGAINST AGE OF EMPIRES 2026-08-17 (owner's request).
Was 0 / 100 / 250 / 400, i.e. 4x a berry bush per farmer at
age 2 rising to 16x at age 4 -- the note here already called
that deliberate rather than measured. Four age-4 plots at 400
is 80 food a tick, about a villager and a half of income every
second, which is not an economy so much as the absence of one.
WHAT WAS IMPORTED IS AoE's RATIO, NOT ITS NUMBERS. AoE2 keeps
every food source within a third of every other per villager:
berries 0.31/s, sheep 0.33, farm 0.35, deer and boar 0.41. A
farm is 1.13x a berry bush there -- what separates food sources
is total amount, walking distance and safety, never a
multiplier on the worker. The absolutes cannot come across:
this game's villager gathers 25 per 100 ticks, which is 2.5 a
second against AoE2's 0.31, so the whole economy runs ~7x
faster by design and only the relationships transfer.
So: 25 at age 2 is parity with gathering by hand, 28 at age 3
is AoE2's own farm-over-berries edge, and 32 at age 4 is 1.28x.
A ladder rather than a ramp, and the reason it is nearly flat
is that AoE's farm upgrades (Horse Collar, Heavy Plow, Crop
Rotation) raise a farm's food AMOUNT -- 175, 250, 325, 425 --
and never the rate. A farmer's throughput in AoE2 is 0.35/s
from the first farm to the last. Those upgrades exist to stop
you rebuilding farms, and `amount -1` below already spent that
entire budget: a plot here never needs rebuilding at all.
Fields are still the backbone, and nothing about that changed.
They are the only RENEWABLE food on the map: the debug map's
whole larder is ~1120 food (4 bushes at 80, 3 sheep at 100, one
cow at 500) and a couple of villagers strip it in minutes. Five
slots, no walk to the drop-off, and infinite beats 13% any day.
The yield is the FIELD's and not the farmer's, which is why it lives here and
not in units.json: advancing an age must not be multiplied by which unit
happens to be standing in the crop. Keyed on age as a STAND-IN for the real
trigger -- the owner's rule is 'as research is completed at the mill' , which is
a mill tech (techs.json exists, nothing researches yet, PLAN.md 9.3). When that
lands the numbers stay here and the lookup changes.
